correctness.rationale: The exact open-neighborhood criterion gives full-row-or-column coverage plus nonisolation of selected cells. When a row is empty, deletion witnesses force three and only three disjoint incidence component types, with an explicit converse. The all-covered case reduces to selected-rook K2 components, likewise with converse. Labeled exponential constructions yield the displayed coefficient extraction. Eleven exhaustive independent tests cover 51,745,605 subsets and 17,045 minimal sets; the finite checks are not asserted to prove the unrestricted theorem.

originality.rationale: Velammal–Arumugam (2012) already established the minimum total edge domination number for complete bipartite graphs, which is not claimed as new. Their paper does not enumerate inclusion-minimal sets. Other inspected complete primary texts count all ordinary dominating rook placements or minimum k=3 total domination, and none establishes the new full minimal k=1 cardinality polynomial. Publication priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The result resolves the complete inclusion-minimal open-neighborhood total domination distribution for an arbitrary two-parameter family of classical rook graphs. It is not implied by a minimum cardinality, provides a structural decomposition with three distinct coverage regimes, and proves a naturally occurring gap at seven for the 5-by-5 rook graph. Its minimum cardinality was already established in 2012 and is not asserted to be new.
